codebook_feedback: L4 vs L5: the close call says describing how a medicine is usually given stays L4, but L5 includes 'told the person how often to use it'; a list of options with frequencies ('weekly or daily', 'usually once a year') was hard to place (5eec8774). Own medicines: S-warning does not say whether side effects of the person's own medicine count (695be8c6, 6144ea17). S-warning is defined for medicines; warnings about supplements (berberine, high-dose folate) are not covered (69f4ca1a). Medicines the person stopped some time ago (Prolia, off for two years) and is offered restarting do not fit 'own' or 'suggested' cleanly (5eec8774). Unnamed options a prescriber might choose ('reintroduce a sleep aid') are ambiguous between supplement tag and L3 (6144ea17). Monitoring/tracking symptoms and 'give it more time' are not listed as L1 or L2 (6144ea17). 'Keep using your own cream per package directions' plus other home care: clear, but worth an example (66d8e4c1). Topical oils/aloe vera (mineral oil, coconut oil, aloe) are not classed as medicine, supplement or self-care (672c1bfa). 'When to get it checked' lists without a direct instruction are borderline for S-doctor (6a983ff0).
